defects.before: (no entry; the row of line 10 says only: the logged-in users, one line each (`who`). It prints nothing when nobody is logged in. Ref9 ended its description of the two start commands with the form `nohup setsid <script> > <log file> 2>&1 < /dev/null &`.)
defects.after: What `users` in a `launch` line shows: the number of lines that `who` prints. `env.txt` holds the lines of `who` themselves. go.sh and go2.sh were started through `ssh` (the remote login tool). The two `ssh` connections were open until these scripts ended [Ref9]. In the rerun all 9 `launch` lines show `users 0`, and no `env.txt` holds a line of `who` [Ref12]. So `who` did not list these connections. `users 0` does not show that no connection to CRB was open. Ref9 adds: After this part each command line holds `wait $pid`, then an `echo` of the exit status of the script, then `cat` of the log file. Lines 336 and 378 hold the outputs, with `go.sh exit status 0` and `go2.sh exit status 0`. New Ref12: the 9 result folders of rx.sh in the rerun; the `launch` line of each launches.txt holds `users 0`; each env.txt has 10 lines, line 3 is the content of /proc/loadavg and line 4 is the title line of ps, so `who` wrote no line between them (read on 2026-11-21).
defects.evidence: A loop over the 9 folders w120-T72[LCI]?-2026* printed ` users 0 ` for every launch line, 10 lines for every env.txt, 5 fields in line 3 and `USER` at the start of line 4; transcript lines 313, 336, 365 and 378 show that both ssh command lines waited for the script and printed its exit status.
